slides.3.title: Features of the Távora-Varosa DOC
slides.3.html:
The Távora-Varosa DOC lies in north-central Portugal. It is the highest-altitude wine region in Portugal and the first sparkling wine DOC.

🏔️ Geography and climate

  • Highlands south of the Douro and north of the Dão, at 500–900m
  • Continental climate with cool summers, cold winters and large day-night temperature swings
  • Soils: granite and schist, poor and well drained
  • High altitude ensures slow ripening and high acidity, ideal conditions for quality sparkling wine

🫧 The birth of a sparkling wine DOC

  • In 1989, Távora-Varosa became Portugal's first official sparkling wine DOC
  • Traditional method (Método Clássico), with second fermentation in bottle
  • A minimum of 18 months on the lees (higher than the Bairrada standard)
  • Main grapes: Malvasia Fina・Gouveio (Verdelho)・Cerceal・Arinto

🍾 Representative producers

  • Murganheira: Portugal's largest producer of traditional-method sparkling wine and the benchmark for Távora-Varosa
  • Caves Aliança: a large wine house and important Espumante producer

slides.4.explanation: In 1989, Távora-Varosa became Portugal's first officially recognised sparkling wine (Espumante) DOC. High altitude (500–900m) and a continental climate ensure high acidity, and the wines are made by the traditional method (Método Clássico) with a minimum of 18 months on the lees.
